title: Lynx Platform - savings reconciliation, workload breakdown, and operational risks
body:
Purpose:
This is an internal reconciliation and operational-risk memo summarizing the before/after cost model for Lynx Platform following Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal is to validate the spreadsheet assumptions, flag operational risks, and provide a prioritized rollout checklist for the Solutions and SRE teams.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline (customer-provided telemetry): ~1.8B tokens/month (inference), 64M embedding vectors/month.
- Baseline hosted spend estimate (customer billing): $98,400/month.
- Redwood Optimize projected (expected scenario): $55,100/month -> ~44% savings.
- Conservative scenario (lower batching, slower adoption of caching): $69,300/month -> ~30% savings.
- Aggressive scenario (full batching + KV prefix caching + 4-bit quantized model): $46,700/month -> ~53% savings.
- Key operational risks: accuracy regressions from quantization, increased tail latency during burst traffic, and rollout complexity for mixed-model fallback.

What I reconciled against the customer spreadsheet:
- Token counts: verified event-by-event token distribution (10th/50th/90th percentiles) against sample logs (2025-09 to 2025-11). Their histogram shows heavy long-tail prompts: 12% of requests > 200 tokens, but those account for ~45% of total tokens.
- Model mapping: customer currently using a hosted 13B model flavor. Redwood recommendation: migrate to Redwood-optimized 13B-int8 variant for standard traffic and keep a 13B-fp16 fallback for high-quality/long-context calls.
- Embeddings: lots of small vector requests; recommended local caching for repeated top-1000 documents and batching embeddings per minute window.

Key assumptions in the Optimize model (explicit):
1) Effective batching: mean in-flight batch size = 8 for short requests, 4 for mixed requests.
2) Quantization uplift: int8 gives 2.1x throughput; 4-bit gives 3.6x but with 1.5–3.0% quality delta on rouge/accuracy for this customer test prompts.
3) KV/prefix caching: avoids compute for the first N tokens of common prompts; estimated hit-rate = 22% after 3 weeks of live usage.
4) Routing & fallback: policy sends latency-sensitive calls to warm fp16 pool; cost modeled as small percent premium for those requests.

Before / After reconciliation table (simplified):
- Baseline compute token cost: $72,100/month
- Baseline embedding cost: $18,000/month
- Baseline infra/other: $8,300/month

Optimize (expected scenario):
- Compute w/ int8 + batching: $40,000/month
- Embedding reduced via batching+cache: $11,000/month
- Infra + overhead (Dedicated buffer + SLO ops): $4,100/month
- Total: $55,100/month

Variance calls and reasons:
- Difference vs customer estimate: Our baseline compute is slightly higher; customer reported aggressive request coalescing that we could not reproduce in their sampled logs. We flagged two endpoints where client-side coalescing reduces token counts by ~8% in their internal dashboard but those calls were not present in logs shared.
- Embeddings variance: customer used a different pricing tier in their sheet (enterprise discount). We matched to their contract tier in the final projection.

Scenario sensitivity (quick):
- If KV cache hit-rate stays below 10% (worst-case), savings drop to ~26% (cost $72k/mo).
- If 4-bit quantization is adopted without rollback and quality regression is >3%, we model a 10% business impact risk (customer churn / reduced usage) — qualitative estimate, requires monitoring.

Operational risks and mitigations (prioritized):
1) Quality regression from quantization: run a blind A/B on a daily prompt-sample set (5k prompts) with automatic BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim thresholds. If delta > 1.8% on primary customer metric, auto rollback. (Owner: Applied ML)
2) Tail latency spikes during autoscale/traffic bursts: ensure canary warm-up for larger batch pools and enable quick-burst reserved capacity for 30s windows. (Owner: SRE / Dedicated infra)
3) Incorrect client-side batching assumptions: add instrumentation to client SDK to emit pre-request batching signals (optional header) to verify real-world coalescing. (Owner: DevX)
4) Embedding cache staleness: TTL policy and invalidation hooks tied to content update webhooks. (Owner: Solutions Eng)

Recommended rollout plan (minimal viable safe rollout):
- Week 0: run offline regression tests with 10k customer prompts across int8 and 4-bit inferences, record metric deltas.
- Week 1: enable int8 for 20% of traffic (non-critical endpoints) + enable embedding batching for background jobs. Monitor quality metrics hourly.
- Week 2-3: increase int8 traffic to 60% conditional on stable metrics; enable KV prefix caching on one high-repeat endpoint and measure hit-rate.
- Week 4: enable conservative autoscaling for burst windows and add fp16 warm pool for latency-sensitive routes.
- Post-rollout (30 days): run full reconciliation vs billing to validate realized savings and adjust model parameters.

Actionable items for Solutions Engineering (short):
- Export the 90-day token-level logs for endpoint "convo-stream" and "summarize-batch" (need by 2026-02-21).
- Push small client SDK patch to tag batching headers by request type (patch PR-421).
- Create a daily eval job in the Optimize harness using the customer-provided metric set.

Open questions / items to confirm with customer:
- Confirm enterprise discount on embeddings (doc: legal/contract clause 5.4) — impacts embedding delta.
- Which endpoints are officially latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive? Need list to map fallback policies.
- Acceptable rollback thresholds for automated quantization failures.

Appendix A — Quick math snapshot (numbers rounded):
- Baseline monthly tokens: 1,800,000,000 tokens
- Baseline token compute unit cost assumed: $0.00004/token -> $72,000
- Int8 effective unit cost: $0.000022/token -> $39,600
- Embedding baseline unit: $0.00028/embedding -> $17,920
- Embedding after batching/cache: $0.00015/embedding -> $9,600

Appendix B — Risk dashboard signals to add to Console: (for SRE / Product)
- Daily mean delta on primary metric (customer-provided) between baseline and optimized cohort
- KV cache hit-rate per endpoint (rolling 7d)
- Fraction of requests hitting fp16 fallback (should be <10% after week 3)
- Tail p95/p99 latency for optimized pool compared to baseline

Notes to self / working questions (raw):
- Customer claims a "client-side aggregator" for embeddings that batches 200/s locally; we need sample traces to validate.
- Consider offering a managed embedding cache add-on for customers with high repetition patterns (commercially potentially valuable).
- Flagging for AM: schedule a quick sync with legal about embeddings discounts and invoice reconciliation timeline.

If this doc looks good, next step is to convert the final reconciliation numbers into the shared spreadsheet tab "lynx-reconcile-v1" (linked in the PR) and schedule the 30-min review with Lynx Product ops.
